title: Irish Breakfast Fry-Up
subtitle: Bacon, sausage, black pudding, eggs, and soda bread on one plate.
description: Adapted from classic full Irish breakfast tradition for firehall griddle service: back bacon, pork sausages, black pudding, grilled tomato, sautéed mushrooms, fried eggs, and soda bread fried in butter for eight hearty plates.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Irish Breakfast Fry-Up in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Cook sausages and pudding
steps.instruction: Brown sausages in a large skillet over medium heat, turning until internal temperature reaches 160°F, about 12 minutes. Add black pudding slices last 4 minutes— they fall apart if overcooked. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Fry bacon and tomatoes
steps.instruction: In a second pan, fry back bacon until edges curl and fat renders. Add tomato halves cut-side down and cook until charred. Hold meats warm on a tray covered loosely with foil. Target 165°F at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Sauté mushrooms
steps.instruction: Sauté mushrooms in butter over high heat without crowding until deeply browned and moisture evaporates. Season with salt and pepper; hold warm. Target 165°F at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Toast soda bread
steps.instruction: Fry soda bread slices in butter until golden on both sides, about 2 minutes per side. Keep crisp on a rack in a 200°F oven. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Fry eggs and plate
steps.instruction: Fry eggs in clean butter over medium until whites are set (165°F) and yolks are runny. Build each plate with sausage, pudding, bacon, tomato, mushrooms, bread, and an egg. Serve immediately. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Run two skillets in parallel—one for meats, one for veg and eggs—to hit eight plates together.
Add black pudding last; it crumbles if it sits on high heat too long.
Plate assembly is fastest if all components are lined on a warm tray before eggs fry.
cleanupNotes: Deglaze sausage pans with hot water while warm—pork fat sets hard once cooled.
Wipe black pudding residue immediately; blood sausage stains boards if left to dry.
leftovers: Reheat meats on a sheet pan at 350°F for 8 minutes; fry fresh eggs to order.
Chop leftovers into a bubble-and-squeak-style potato hash for the next breakfast.
